title: Valmiki's GOAT checklist

verse.sanskrit:
कोन्वस्मिन्साम्प्रतं लोके गुणवान्कश्च वीर्यवान् ।
धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च सत्यवाक्यो दृढव्रतः ॥
verse.iast:
ko nv asmin sāmprataṃ loke guṇavān kaś ca vīryavān |
dharmajñaś ca kṛtajñaś ca satyavākyo dṛḍhavrataḥ ||
verse.translation: Who in this world today is virtuous and also valiant, knows dharma, is grateful, truthful and firm in his vows?

beats.title: a GOAT checklist
beats.vo: The Ramayana literally opens with a question. Valmiki asks the sage Narada: who is the greatest person alive right now?
And his checklist is not followers or flexes. Number one: brave, yes, but also grateful, truthful, and true to his word.
Number two: good character, and kind to every living being. Not just the ones who can do something for you.
Number three: self-controlled, has conquered anger, and is never jealous of anyone.
Who in the world today is virtuous and brave, knows what's right, is grateful, truthful and firm in his vows?

beats.title: Narada's answer?
beats.vo: Narada says: there is one. Rama, of the Ikshvaku family. Deep as the ocean, steady as the Himalaya.

beats.title: Your character is the flex
beats.vo: The greatest story ever told starts by rating character, not clout. Run your own checklist.

caption:
The Ramayana opens with a GOAT checklist 🐐

Valmiki's first question to Narada: who in this world is virtuous and brave, grateful, truthful, kind to every being, free of anger and envy? Narada's answer: Rama, deep as the ocean and steady as the Himalaya (1.17).

“कोन्वस्मिन्साम्प्रतं लोके गुणवान्कश्च वीर्यवान् । धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च सत्यवाक्यो दृढव्रतः ॥”
Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 1.2 (with 1.3–4, 1.8, 1.17)
